specs.anchorText: The inside leaks out: a closed curve that fails to enclose anything.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette, on a clean white background with generous margins: a ring of dark rounded square pixel-blocks arranged as a diamond fence, each block touching its neighbors only at the corners, leaving little diagonal gaps. A small worried cartoon water droplet (or a tiny ghost) that was supposed to be trapped inside the diamond is happily squeezing sideways through one of the diagonal corner gaps and escaping to the outside, looking pleased with itself. A second tiny character standing inside looks surprised that the fence is not actually sealed. Gentle humor about a fence that looks closed but leaks at the corners. Friendly XKCD-inspired style, expressive, minimal clutter, suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the composition simple and focused on one clear visual metaphor.
specs.alt: A diamond-shaped fence of pixel blocks that touch only at their corners, with a small trapped character slipping sideways through a diagonal corner gap and escaping to the outside, illustrating the digital Jordan curve paradox where an 8-connected closed loop fails to truly enclose its interior.
specs.caption: A loop that looks closed can still leak: this corner-gap escape is why foreground and background must be given complementary connectivities.

specs.anchorText: Fit shrinks, hit grows; min versus max; pessimist versus optimist.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette, on a clean white background with generous margins, split into two gentle halves. Left half: a small grumpy cartoon stamp character labeled by its glum expression, pressing a round cookie-cutter probe onto a soft blob and only keeping the part where the whole cutter fits fully inside, so the blob shrinks and a tiny speck nearby vanishes; the character looks skeptical and cautious. Right half: a cheerful optimistic cartoon stamp character pressing the same round probe and keeping every spot it merely touches, so the blob puffs up bigger and a little notch fills in; the character looks delighted and generous. The two are clearly twins with opposite moods. Friendly XKCD-inspired style, expressive faces, minimal clutter, suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the composition simple and focused on one clear visual metaphor.
specs.alt: Two twin cartoon characters pressing the same round probe onto a blob: a cautious pessimist who keeps only where the probe fits entirely inside, shrinking the shape and deleting a speck, and a cheerful optimist who keeps anywhere the probe touches, growing the shape and filling a notch, mapping erosion to a hard minimum and dilation to a hard maximum.
specs.caption: Erosion is the pessimist asking does my probe fit inside, dilation the optimist asking does it touch anywhere: that single contrast is almost all of morphology.

specs.alt: A cartoon factory assembly line where a noisy dark blob speckled with specks and pinholes enters, one robot worker brushes away the small specks (opening), the next patches the small holes (closing), and a clean blob rolls off to a counting-and-measuring station, depicting the standard open-then-close mask cleanup pipeline.
specs.caption: One operator's destruction is the other's restoration: opening deletes what is too small to matter, closing fills what is too small to be a real hole, and a clean mask rolls off ready to count.
